arguments.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: complete-frame 2D fighting-game RUN STOP sprite sheet. Generate exactly12 fully finished Sora KH2 poses in a strict4-column by3-row grid, chronological left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Use a large landscape canvas, equal-sized cells, true transparent alpha background and generous padding. Every entire figure, Kingdom Key and chain stays inside its own cell, with no overlap into adjacent cells. No text, labels, borders, checkerboard, colored backdrop, ambient glow, motion blur or effects. Each cell is one complete illustration; no individual component layers.
Image roles: image1 is the accepted run-start sheet and sets the polished smooth clean 2D cel-shaded art style and exact KH2 outfit. Image2 is the newly generated run loop: keep its same Sora model, face, hair size, curved cloth volumes, anatomy, rich shoes and weapon finish; its TOP LEFT pose is this stop sequence's initial pose. Ignore any preview background colors. Image3 is the accepted low ready pose and is the final pose target, keeping its detailed clothing and two-hand braced guard. Image4 is ONLY the photographic same-arm shoulder-carry and rigid weapon geometry reference, not the clothing or rendering style.
Sora faces RIGHT at a constant three-quarter camera angle. Consistent youthful face, brown spiky hair silhouette, black/silver KH2 jacket, red waist cloth, crossed yellow straps, baggy dark shorts, black gloves and oversized black/red/yellow shoes. Stable body scale, head size and limb lengths throughout. Genuine progressive articulated movement, with smooth small pose changes and no repeated/scaled copies.
Twelve stop phases:0 exactly match image2's first/top-left running contact pose, near/front foot forward planted and far leg trailing, far arm carrying weapon over its far shoulder;1 bend front knee and compress to brake, rear foot starts catching up;2 rear knee swings toward body as weight remains on planted front sole;3 rear foot catches and plants while torso begins rising;4 both feet support a controlled recovery with momentum decreasing;5 far holding arm lifts the blade just clear of that same shoulder;6 raise the rigid weapon to an upright clearance pose without passing through head;7 begin lowering and rotating the same held weapon toward the forward low guard, empty front hand approaches;8 far holding wrist continues down and front hand approaches the guard without swapping the holding arm;9 front hand joins to brace as feet settle into image3's stance;10 near-final low ready pose with slight residual body/cloth/chain motion;11 settle into the image3 ready stance, feet grounded, connected weapon diagonally pointing back-left/up from the hands. Finish once, not a loop. Front support foot remains planted through braking; rear foot takes one controlled catch/recovery step into the final stance. Torso bob, hip/shoulder rotation and counterbalance remain coherent; cloth and chain trail then settle.
Weapon invariants: from0 through shoulder clearance, the FAR/REAR arm holds the Kingdom Key over that SAME far shoulder behind the head, and the NEAR/FRONT arm has an empty hand. The far hand retains the handle during the full recovery; the near hand only assists at the end. Correct wrist/thumb/knuckle orientation, never an upside-down grip. One identical Kingdom Key throughout: gold rectangular guard surrounds black handle; attached blue/silver collar joins one straight silver shaft to one crown/key-tooth terminal. Same geometry, length and projected thickness in every frame; all weapon elements rotate together as one rigid object. No broken, duplicated, bent or reversed blade and no detached guard or handle. Keep coherent head/body occlusion and a slight consistent foreground tip projection during carry. Chain stays attached at the pommel and settles naturally. Match source1/source2 art quality in ALL12 poses.
